handoff: B20 (a tick never creates a label) is untraced: add a tick test asserting no label+/labels? calls. Minor: doctor ok not asserted (B16/B18), label names unquoted in printed commands, loose glab 409 match. Everything else traced and green.

findings.title: B20 is UNTRACED: no test shows a tick never creates a label
findings.detail:
Spec B20: "`norn:wf:reproduce` is missing and a `reproduce` round starts → the label swap warns as today (RD5); no label is created by the tick." GR10: "Only `init` and `upgrade` create labels; a tick never does." The code holds: only init, upgrade and doctor call remoteLabels (packages/cli/src/runtime/labels.ts:45). But no test asserts it. FakeRemote records `label+ <name>` and `labels?` in `calls` (test/support/harness.ts), and no tick test checks those calls are absent.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a CLI-seam test in labels.test.ts: inited repo, remove norn:wf:reproduce from h.remote.labels, start a round with that workflow (story edit --workflow reproduce) and tick. Assert the RD5 swap warning, and that h.remote.calls holds no `label+` and no `labels?` entry from the tick.

findings.title: doctor's 'not a failure' is claimed in test names but not asserted
findings.detail:
B16/B18: "the overall result is not a failure". The doctor tests check the warnings but never doctor's `ok` or its exit code. The code doesn't feed labels into `ok` (doctor.ts:643), so the item holds, but a regression would go unseen.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert that the labels warning alone does not flip `ok`. For example, compare `ok` with a run where the remote has every label, or assert that `labels` is not in the ok expression's inputs by checking `ok` stays equal across both runs.

findings.title: GitLab parity is covered only at the port and command level
findings.detail:
B3: "the same labels exist on the GitLab project; the report reads as on GitHub." FakeRemote is fixed to provider gh, so no CLI test runs init against glab. The glab adapter passes the RemotePort contract over a scripted glab, and labelCreateCommand/labelDeleteCommand('glab') are unit-tested. The implementer recorded this as a decision.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Acceptable as recorded. Optionally let FakeRemote take a provider, and add one init test on glab that asserts the glab create/delete commands in the report.

findings.title: B14's 'everything else stays done' and B15's not-checked/unused JSON are not asserted
findings.detail:
The B14 test only checks the labels line. The B15 JSON is asserted for created/existing/not_created, but not for the `checked: false` shape or for `unused`.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add `--json` asserts to the B11/B14 and B8/B10 tests.

findings.title: Label names are not shell-quoted in printed create/delete commands
findings.detail:
The description goes through quoted(), but the name does not: `gh label create ${label.name} …`, `glab label create --name ${label.name}`, `label delete ${name}` (lines 86-87, 92). The intake label comes from config (`label: NonEmpty`, packages/schema/src/config.ts:151), so `label: needs triage` prints a command that creates the wrong label. quoted() also leaves `!` alone, which triggers history expansion when pasted into an interactive bash.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Quote the name like the description, and prefer single-quoting (escape ' as '\'') to avoid `!` expansion.

findings.title: glab `_exists` match on a bare '409' over stdout+stderr is too loose
findings.detail:
`/already exists|409|has already been taken/i` runs over `${r.stderr}${r.stdout}`, so any failing output containing 409 (an id, a URL) becomes glab_exists. remoteLabels then counts the label as already there (runtime/labels.ts:72), which hides a create that failed.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Anchor the match to `HTTP 409` or `409 Conflict`, or to the 'has already been taken' message.

findings.title: Small smells in runtime/labels.ts and its callers
findings.detail:
(1) `norn:wf:${w}` hardcodes the prefix where core uses WF_LABEL. (2) The B5 `not_created.command` holds `norn doctor`, while elsewhere the field holds a create command, so it means two things in --json. (3) `_auth` on create is always reported as 'permission denied', even when the CLI logged out. (4) init strips the 'labels: ' prefix that labelsLines just added (init.ts ~123). (5) `UpgradeReport.labels?` is optional but every path sets it. (6) glab lists one page of 100 labels, so doctor can warn a false 'missing' beyond it.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optional cleanups; none needs a round on its own.
